Notes in: which input and channel play notes and knobs (the others are ignored, so gear that sends its own notes or echoes ours can't play the pads). Keys play: in the tracker a keyboard plays the instrument you're on (a MIDI instrument plays its gear, with bend, mod wheel, aftertouch and sustain passed through); or the pads, as on the Synth page. Instruments set to MIDI (INST › OUTPUT) play on their PORT (A–D) and channel. Pick which cable each port is here: the song keeps only the letter, so it plays the same on the phone and the computer with each one's own gear. Delay (per port): how long that gear takes to sound after a note; raise it if the gear sounds late against ...Thunder, lower it if early. Clock out sends tempo, Start and Stop to the ports lit (A–D) while the song plays (from partway into the song: Song Position Pointer and Continue). Clock in follows another device's clock: its Start and Stop run PLAY (Continue after a Song Position Pointer plays from there), and its tempo sets ours. Clock from: the input to follow; the first one keeps it until it goes quiet, so two devices sending clock can't double the tempo.

Plug a controller in (USB-C on the phone), tap Connect MIDI, and pads 00–07 answer notes 36–43; other notes play the selected synth. Tap Learn, then: tap any pad (drums or synths) and hit a key to give it that note, or touch any slider and turn a knob to put it on that knob. A knob works the slider for whichever pad, layer or effect is open. Select a pad or slider in Learn and tap Unlearn to clear it.

Latency and rate change when audio restarts. That reloads ...Thunder; your song and kit are kept.

Output picks where everything plays: the synth, the tracker and previews. Level is the overall volume after the tracker’s master. Lowest latency answers the pads fastest; Safest uses a bigger buffer if you hear crackles. Rate: Device uses the output’s own rate.

Getting started

...Thunder has four screens: the Synth, where you build an 8-pad kit; the Tracker, a sequencer that plays that kit; …waves, a modular synth that plays as a layer oscillator; and …chains, where you design modular effects chains for the tracker’s tracks (Mixer → CHN). Switch at the top. ⚙ Settings → App → Mobile turns the app into ...Thunder for phones: Synth and Tracker only, with PAD input. …waves layers and …chains effects still play there, so the same files work in both. Everything saves in the browser as you work; File ▾ saves a project file (song and kit) you can keep or move to another device, and opens, renders and exports. There is also a desktop app for Windows, Mac and Linux (github.com/matthettich/thunder-plus/releases/latest) that keeps itself up to date; it keeps its own songs and kits, so use File to move work between it and the browser.

How a song fits together

Song (256 rows × 8–32 tracks of sect numbers, 16 to start) → Sect (up to 16 phrases, each with a transpose) → Phrase (up to 32 rows of note, volume, instrument and three effects) → Inst (which pad a note plays, with transpose, volume, pan, reverse and start). Mixer, FX and Project sit around them.

Starting a new song resets the pattern numbering to 00. Project → › NEW SONG (EDIT×2) or › LOAD DEMO begins with its first block at 00; the numbers never carry over from the previous song.

Sects are hidden by default (⚙ Settings → Hide sect page, or Project → SECT): EDIT×2 on an empty song cell makes a block that already holds a phrase, SHIFT+▶ opens that phrase, and EDIT×2 on a filled block makes a unique copy. Set SECT to SHOWN for the sect screen; nothing is lost either way.

PLAY in Song starts from the block under the cursor, or from the top when the cell under the cursor is empty.

The Song screen is Arrange. Every song row is a row of blocks, one column per track, with the amber MST column at the right. Everything the Song screen does works the same: the keys, the pad and command buttons, typing hex, EDIT×2, selecting, copy and paste. On the other screens Arrange moves to its place at the right when there is room (wide screens). To go back to the text grid, tick Settings → Show classic Song screen.

Arrange (wide screens): the overview at the right shows the whole song, lined up with the Song screen (scroll either one and the other follows). A tap on a block goes to it (a second tap opens its phrase). Holding a block (touch or pen) mutes or unmutes just that one; with a mouse, Alt-click or middle-click it — the phrase stays in place, silent, so you can drop parts in and out while arranging. Tap a row number to play from there; in KEYS mode M mutes the block under the Song cursor. Whole tracks are muted in the Mixer, never here, so a slip can’t silence a track.

The screens are laid out as a map: Song ▶ Sect ▶ Phrase ▶ Inst left to right, Project above, Mixer below, FX to the right of the Mixer. You move between them with the screen keys below, the tabs, or the map in the side panel.

Pluck string

A layer type (Layer → Type → Pluck string): a Karplus–Strong plucked string. A burst of noise rings round a delay one period long, losing its top end as it goes, so it sounds like a guitar, harp or koto string. Bright sets the pluck and how fast the highs fade; Decay how long it rings. Give the layer's Amp a long decay (or sustain) so the string can ring out. In …waves the String module is the same string with a Gate to pluck it, a pick Position and a Mute for when the note ends.

Blip engine

Synth → Engine: Blip (any pad, drums too) turns a pad into a minimal electronic drum, in the spirit of the generative blip grooveboxes: a parabolic tone with a Kick (a fast pitch drop; Kick time sets how fast), FM (and its ratio), Ring mod (slow is a tremolo, fast is metal), Noise and Click, then Decay, Drive, a Filter (left of centre low-pass, right high-pass) and Grain (the hit repeated, each quieter: a stutter). Presets go from Click and Boom to Metal, Tick hat and Glitch; Random rolls a new one. In …chains and …waves, the Blip drum module plays eight of these voices and the Life module sequences them.

Voice engine

Synth → Engine: Voice turns a synth slot (9–16) into a singing robot. Type the lyrics: each note the tracker plays sings the next syllable (its consonants on the attack, the vowel held until the note ends), and PLAY starts the lyrics again from the top. A slide keeps the syllable it's on, for runs over one vowel. The chips under the lyrics show every syllable as the engine will say it. If a word comes out wrong, split it with a hyphen (to-night) or spell it in brackets with ARPAbet sounds: [HH EH L OW] (AA AE AH AO AW AY EH ER EY IH IY OW OY UH UW AX; B CH D DH F G HH JH K L M N NG P R S SH T TH V W Y Z ZH). Robot goes from a natural voice to a buzzy one, Size changes the voice's size (bigger is deeper), Voice at 0 whispers, Diction speeds the consonants up or slows them down. A full stop, comma, ; : ! ? or _ is a rest: that note (or pad step) is silent, so hello . world pauses between the words and several in a row pause longer. Consonant noise sets how loud the hiss of K, T, P, S and H is, and Clarity narrows the formants and lifts their presence so words are easier to make out. The pad (and exports) sing the whole line, one syllable every Pad step. One voice per track (mono).

Bass engine

Any synth slot (08 and up) can be a bass instead of layers: on the Synth page pick Engine: Bass. It is an additive mono bass in the spirit of Reaktor's Lazerbass, for dubstep and drum & bass: up to 64 partials (Shape goes saw › square › triangle; Bright, Odd / even, Stretch), a sub oscillator, a resonant low-pass with its own envelope, vowel formants, a comb, Reese detune and stereo Width. The Wobble moves the cutoff, vowel, comb and level at a rate locked to the song's tempo (4 bars down to 1/32, triplets and dotted). In the tracker it plays live, so the wobble keeps time on every note however high you play, a held note wobbles for as long as it's held, and Glide and Legato slide between notes (PSL slides without restarting). The WOB command changes the rate from a row on (WOB 06 = 1/4, WOB 0B = 1/16, WOB 00 back to the voice's own). Presets get you started; the bottom panel's instrument section shows its level, cutoff, resonance and wobble. The voice's Level, Tune and Drive apply; pad effects don't (use the track's FX).

Levels: TRIM, VOL, MASTER, OUT

Each track runs TRIM → …chains → its FX → VOL (with mute and solo) → pan. TRIM is the Mixer's first row: the track's input gain, 80 = 0 dB, from −18 to +18 dB, set before the chain and effects hear it. It lights yellow under the value when what the track sends in runs hot (above −6 dB) and red near full scale (above −1 dB): …chains has no limiter of its own. VOL is the fader: the bar on each track's meter (drag it, Shift for fine, double-click for 0 dB; from the keyboard, ▼ from the SC row lands on it, then Ctrl/⌘+◀▶ ±1, ▲▼ ±16) and the bottom panel's slider. On the master row, MASTER is the drive into the limiter (the master phrase's VOL moves it), then FX, MASTERING and OUT: the master fader, after the limiter, FF = 0 dB and never a boost. Its bar stands on the L / R meter (drag it sideways) and the bottom panel's master strip is OUT too. Renders and stems go through all of them as you hear them, except that with Project → NORMALISE on the file is then raised to just under 0 dB, so OUT doesn't change its level there (MASTER still drives the limiter). Turning a track's CHN on or off fades between the chain and the dry sound over 20 ms, so it doesn't click.

Buses and PRE sends. A Track In patched into a Chain Out on another track feeds that bus after its fader and pan. Set the Track In's Bus send to Before its fader and the bus hears it after its chain and effects but before VOL and pan, so pulling the fader down leaves the send alone (a reverb or monitor send). Mute and solo still silence it.

Mastering

Settings → Master → Open mastering… (or the MASTERING cell on the Mixer's master row: ▶ from the master level, then EDIT; or › MASTERING on the FX screen's master) puts a chain on the master bus: EQ → Suppress → Compress → Limit. Each has its own switch; the readouts show short-term loudness in and out (LUFS) and the highest peak. EQ: drag a point (left/right is frequency, up/down is gain), shift-drag or scroll for width, double-click empty space to add a bell, double-click a point to switch it off; the band row sets exact values. Suppress turns down resonances that stick out of the spectrum (Depth, Sharpness, Selectivity, Speed; drag the lines to set its range; Delta plays only what it removes). Compress is a glue compressor (its sidechain high-pass keeps the bass from pumping it). Limit catches every peak at the Ceiling, between samples too. Renders of the song include the chain and keep its ceiling; stems don't.

…pump effects

The nine …pump mastering plugins run on bus tracks and the master, and EQ on any track too (FX picker → Mastering (…pump); › EQ WINDOW on the FX screen opens it): EQ (24 bands, cuts to 96 dB/oct or Brickwall, dynamic bands, zero latency or linear phase), COMP, LIMIT (true peak, loudness targets), CALM (resonance suppressor), TONE (tonal balance), BAND (multiband dynamics), WIDE (stereo imager), HEAT (saturator) and METER (loudness). They are the plugins' own DSP, so a setting sounds as it does in the VST3 / CLAP plugin. The slot shows the main settings as hex rows (EQ, BAND, WIDE and HEAT pick a BAND first); › PRESET has the plugin's presets and › OPEN its full window, which works like the plugin: drag, Shift-drag for fine, double-click to type, Ctrl-click to reset, A/B, and Alt held to listen to a band or a range. A slot's ACTIVE is the plugin's bypass. CALM, TONE, LIMIT and linear-phase EQ add latency: renders of the master line it up, but on a bus that track plays late against the others.

Settings

⚙ Settings at the top: it starts with Audio (output device, level, latency, rate), then this screen’s own settings (in the tracker every Project setting: Song, Input, Screen, Render), then Master, Skin, Export, MIDI, Kit and App (Mobile, install, check for update). There you can also turn off Display steps as decimal (row numbers in hex), turn off Play note on entry (audition notes as you type them), show or hide the KEYS-mode on-screen keypad (Settings → KEYS KEYPAD; it starts hidden on a computer and shown in the Mobile setup), and change the Text size of the tracker screen. With the KEYS keypad off, a bottom panel takes its place: a spectrum of the master, quick controls for the current instrument’s sound, the …chains controls you have added for the current track (in …chains, right-click a control or a module → Add to the bottom panel; right-click one in the panel to remove it), the current track’s effects, and a channel strip for the current track (stereo meter, fader with 0 dB at E0 and +6 dB at the top, pan, M and S). When it holds more than fits, the panel scrolls sideways. Tap a section’s button to hide it (it waits as a dashed + button); drag the panel’s top edge for its height and the scope’s or FX section’s edge for their widths. On a big screen the space beside the grid is the stage (Settings → STAGE): BY SCREEN shows something useful for each screen (the dogs dance to the beat on Song and Project — a hop every beat, a bigger one on the bar, and a new dance (arms up, arms down, leg kicks, jumping jacks) every time the cursor’s track starts a phrase, so they count beats and phrases for you — Sect previews the phrase, Phrase shows a piano lighting the notes as they play, Inst the waveform, Mixer the master spectrum, FX the effects chain), DOGS shows the dogs everywhere, OFF leaves it empty. In the bar above the grid, double-click the tempo or LPB to type a new one (ticks a step are in Settings). The panel follows the track the cursor is on: its instrument (on Song, the one the block under the cursor plays), its effects and its strip. When any track is soloed, SOLO · CLEAR shows; ✕ hides the panel and Settings → BOTTOM PANEL brings it back. Drag a finger up or down anywhere on the tracker screen to scroll; drag on the cursor's cell to change its value. With a mouse, a drag selects instead (the wheel scrolls), a selection drags to move (Alt, Ctrl or ⌘ copies), and right-click on a track number solos it: see Tracker · KEYS mode → Mouse.

Project files are .thunder files (.json ones still open). A dot on File ▾ and in the window title means changes that aren't in the file yet; New, Open and the rest ask Save changes? first. The app remembers the file (Ctrl/⌘+S goes back to it after a restart) and File ▾ → Open recent… lists the last eight. Every 3 minutes the song and kit are backed up in the browser, the last 10: File ▾ → Restore a backup…. On Android, tapping a .thunder attachment can’t offer a web app (Android doesn’t give a PWA the custom extension), so either tap Share on the attachment and send it to ...Thunder Plus (install it first: Settings → App), or download it and use LOAD PROJECT; that picker now shows every file. Drop audio on a pad to load it; drop a project, kit or .mid on the window to open it. Sliders all work alike: drag one from where it is (it doesn't jump to the click), hold Shift for fine control; on a touch screen it moves only once your finger slides sideways. Double-click, Alt-click or Ctrl/⌘-click resets it, double-click the value to type one, right-click for Reset / Type a value / MIDI learn. The wheel moves the slider the pointer rests on (it gets an outline); Shift+wheel in fine steps.

Drum pads and synths

The kit has 16 slots to start, up to 64: SLOTS at the top of the Synth page (− and + step by 8, tap the number to type one; fewer slots only hide the last ones, and their sounds come back). THIS SLOT sets how the selected slot plays: ONE-SHOT plays its whole sound, like a drum; HELD sounds until note-off, like a synth. By default: 1–8 are drum pads: one-shots that play their whole sound. 9–16 are synths for melodies and chords (Bass, Pluck, Keys, Pad, Lead, Bell, Organ, Sub to start): a note holds at its sustain level for as long as you hold it, up to the slot’s Max len, then fades over its release when you let go. C-4 plays middle C. In the tracker, instruments 08–0F play the synth slots in a new song. A voice per track (Settings → Kit) grows the kit past 16 slots: every song track gets its own pad — drums on mono tracks, a simple synth on poly ones. The pads stay the same size and scroll up and down.

Chopping breaks

Load a drum loop into a pad (Synth → Load sample), then on its instrument (INST) set SLICES (GRID cuts equal parts, HITS cuts at each drum hit it finds). Each note now plays one slice: C-4 the first, C#4 the second and so on, so you can rearrange the break in a phrase. SYNC fits the loop to the song tempo: set BEATS to how long the loop is (or use › GUESS BEATS). REPITCH changes its speed and pitch together; STRETCH keeps the pitch with smooth grains; LOOP keeps the pitch with little tempo-synced loops for a gritty, stuttery sound (GRAIN sets their length). › PLAY SLICES auditions them in order.

Chords and polyphony

The second half of the tracks is polyphonic (9–16 with 16 tracks, 17–32 with 32; Settings → Song → Tracks): the green POLY box on the right of Song and Mixer. The first half, in the pink MONO box on the left, plays one note at a time. Open a phrase from a polyphonic track and it shows four note columns, N1–N4, so a row can hold a chord. Notes on these tracks ring over each other, up to 4 at a time per track; a fifth steals the oldest. A note OFF in any note column releases everything on the track. The mono tracks stay one note at a time, and a phrase played there uses only N1.

Two input modes

PAD is a d-pad plus SHIFT, PLAY, OPTION and EDIT, good with a thumb. KEYS is direct entry: type notes, hex and effects, with an on-screen keypad on touch screens. The keyboard works in both — in PAD mode Z and X stay OPTION and EDIT and Alt+arrows page; everything else types as in KEYS. Switch with ⚙ Settings → Input (or Project → INPUT).

Main keys

The first six rows work on every page, and so does Space (play or stop the song; Shift Space plays this screen, the selected pad on the Synth page); the rest are the tracker’s.

UNDO · REDOCtrl/⌘ Z · Ctrl/⌘ Shift Z (or Ctrl/⌘ Y)
The command rowEdit ▾ in the top bar, a right-click on the screen, or View ▾ → COMMAND BAR (buttons; hover one for its key)

Moving

arrowsMove the cursor (drops a line selection)
Alt/⌥ ◀ ▶Previous / next screen, in tab order (Song → … → Inst → Mixer → FX → Project); Alt/⌥ ▲ Project, ▼ Mixer. From Phrase, Alt/⌥+◀ gives Arrange the keys. Option moves, Command edits
Alt/⌥ AGive Arrange the keys from any screen; the screen beside it (Mixer, FX, a phrase…) stays. Again, or Esc, gives them back to it
Tab / Shift TabIn a phrase: note → instrument → FX1 → FX2 → FX3 and round again (Shift: back); the other note columns and volume are on the arrows. Elsewhere: the next / previous track
Home End PgUp PgDnTop, bottom, 16 rows up or down
Shift Alt arrowsIn a phrase: one Song cell up / down on this track (▲▼) or left / right on this row (◀▶), empty cells too (an empty one opens a fresh phrase that goes on the Song with its first note); Arrange scrolls to keep it in view. On the Song: jump to the next block that way, or one cell when there is none. The same from the Mixer and FX screens (the Mixer's master row is ▼ past the VOL faders)
[ ]Previous / next sect, phrase, instrument or FX track, by number
◀ ▶ on the FX screenOpen the slot's controls · back to the slot list
Mouse wheelScroll the screen a row at a time

Typing

Z S X … ;Notes, lower octave (S D G H J are the sharps; the E above is on the upper row, as / mutes the track); on tracks 9–16, → to N2–N4 to add chord notes
Q 2 W … PNotes, upper octave
1 or Caps LockNote off
− = or numpad / *Octave down / up
0–9 A–FHex values: two digits, or one for an instrument
LettersCommands in FX columns (press again to cycle through the commands starting with it: R gives RET, REP, RND, RNL, RTG, RES)
{ }Edit step down / up: how far the cursor moves after you type
Ctrl/⌘ arrowsChange the value (◀▶ by 1, ▲▼ by more); on the Mixer's FX row, turn a track's effects on (▲▶) or off (▼◀), up to eight
EnterAdd, open, or run a › row · twice for a new sect or phrase · in a phrase, on a filled note, picks up that note and its instrument as the current ones, so Enter on an empty note adds them (until you've chosen an instrument, new notes take the highest instrument number already in the phrase); on an instrument, volume or effect, picks it up as the current value (shown after NOW on the hint line); on an empty effect cell it writes the current effect, and Enter twice on an effect cell opens the effect list

Rows

Delete BackspaceClear the cell under the cursor, or the whole highlighted selection. In a phrase, Backspace then steps down (by the edit step)
Shift Delete Shift BackspaceClear the whole row, then step down
InsertAdd a blank row (rows below move down)
Ctrl/⌘ BackspaceRemove the row (rows below move up)

Selecting, copy and paste

Shift arrowsSelect cells from the cursor in Song, Sect and Phrase: ▲▼ straight up and down, ◀▶ sideways; keep Shift held to grow the block. On a line selection, Shift+▲▼ grows the lines and Shift+◀▶ turns them into a block (on screens with nothing to select they move like plain arrows; Alt/⌥ arrows change screen)
Ctrl/⌘ Shift ▲ ▼Select whole lines in Song, Sect and Phrase. The first press takes the cursor’s line, the next ones grow it (in PAD mode too). Elsewhere they change the value, like Ctrl/⌘ arrows
Ctrl/⌘ ASelect every line
Ctrl/⌘ BStart a block selection; arrows grow it
Ctrl/⌘ C Ctrl/⌘ XCopy / cut the selection
Ctrl/⌘ VPaste at the cursor row, or over a selection from its top. Lines paste into any phrase
EscDrop the selection
Row numbersTap or click one to select that line; another to grow the selection to it

Mouse

DragSelect a block, from any cell. Past the top or bottom of the grid it scrolls on
Shift clickSelect from the cursor to here; Shift-click again to grow or shrink it
Drag a selectionMove it. Hold Alt/⌥, Ctrl or ⌘ as you let go to copy it. One undo step; Esc while dragging puts it back
Alt/⌥ dragChange the value of the cell it starts on (a plain drag selects, from any cell); add Ctrl/⌘ for big steps (an octave, 16), Shift for a slower drag. On the Song an Alt-click mutes the block (inside a selection: every block in it)
WheelMove a row per notch
Right-clickThe Edit commands; on a track number or meter it solos the track (again un-solos). A click mutes
Double-click a track numberName and colour the track (or Edit ▾ → Name this track…)
Pattern view bandAlt-click mutes the track, right-click solos it, a click opens it
ArrangeAlt-click or middle-click mutes a block, or every block in the selection when you click inside it; Ctrl/⌘- or Alt-drag copies; double-click an empty cell for a new phrase
Ctrl/⌘ Shift VMix-paste: only into empty cells

Selection tools

Edit ▾ / right-clickInterpolate (a ramp between the first and last selected rows), Volume… (scale, fade, set), Instrument… (set, swap), Shrink, Expand. The selection, or the whole phrase
Render to a slot…The phrase selection, the phrase, or song rows in Arrange, rendered into a kit slot as its sample (or as a WAV)

Playing

SpacePlay or stop the song from the cursor row, on every screen (the Synth page too)
Shift SpacePlay or stop this screen: the phrase (on the Song, the block’s phrase), the sect; on a bus’s phrase or sect (Pattern view too), its song row with every track that feeds it, looping. On the Synth page, the selected pad
Ctrl SpacePlay just this pattern (the song row, every track), looped: turns LOOP on and plays; again stops and turns LOOP off (⌘ Space works too if Spotlight isn’t on it)
/ or \Mute or unmute the track you’re on (the whole track, as the mixer’s M; M on the Song mutes one block)
Ctrl/⌘ / or \Solo the track you’re on (again: un-solo it) · with Shift, clear every solo
Alt LLoop the pattern (LOOP): the song repeats the row it is on. Shift Alt L loops the selection (LOOP SEL): PLAY then loops those rows
Alt , Alt .Transpose the phrase selection down / up a semitone

Tracker · PAD mode

ArrowsMove
SHIFT + ◀▶Change screen (through every screen in tab order)
SHIFT + ▲▼In Song, Sect and Phrase: select the cursor's line, then grow the selection a line at a time (OPTION copies, OPTION+EDIT cuts). On the other screens: Project / Mixer
EDITAdd, or run a › row · in a phrase, on a filled note stamps the current note and instrument over it; on an instrument, volume or effect, picks it up · tap twice for a new sect or phrase, or a note off
EDIT + arrowsChange the value (◀▶ by 1, ▲▼ by more)
OPTION + EDITClear (with a selection: cut)
OPTION + arrowsOther sect, phrase, instrument or FX track · on the Mixer's FX row, turn a track's effects on (▲▶) or off (▼◀) · in Song, page up/down
OPTION + arrows in PhraseGo to the phrase above / below on this track (▲▼) or to the left / right on this row (◀▶), as laid out on the Song grid. A phrase not in the song steps by number. (Settings → Input → PATTERN NAV; off: ▲▼ jump 16 phrases)
SHIFT + OPTION + arrowsIn the Song grid: jump to the next / previous phrase on this row (◀▶), or the same track's phrase above / below (▲▼) — the same in KEYS mode
SHIFT + OPTIONStart or cancel a selection; arrows grow it, OPTION copies
SHIFT + EDITPaste
PLAY · SHIFT + PLAYPlay this screen · play the song · with LOOP on, PLAY loops the selected rows
LOOP · SEMI +/−Loop the selection (sticky) · transpose the phrase selection ±1 semitone at once
◀ ▶ on the FX screenOpen a slot's controls · back to the slot list (a sideways swipe does it too)
EDIT on an FX slotA list of every effect (like the FX command list): pick one and its controls open; its own effect, marked NOW, keeps its settings; --- empties the slot
Row numbersTap to select whole lines, then COPY and PASTE

One finger is enough. With Sticky keys on, tap SHIFT or OPTION alone and it stays lit for the next button. The command row (Project → COMMANDS) gives every two-key command its own button: change, prev/next, clear, select, copy, cut, paste, play song, and on the SONG screen CLN↓ (clones the block, or the selected blocks, into new numbers on a new row below; the rows below move down) and CLN (clone): the block under the cursor is copied, phrases and all, to the next free number.

On a computer keyboard in PAD mode the keyboard is not disabled: arrows move, Enter opens, Space plays, typing letters and hex edits the cell, and Shift selects lines (so does Ctrl/⌘ Shift ▲▼, as in KEYS mode). Z stays OPTION (not a note), X stays EDIT, and Alt+arrows page (OPTION+arrow) rather than change the value.

Touch

Tap a cell to move there; tap it again to open or add. Drag up or down on the cursor’s cell to change its value; drag elsewhere to scroll.

FX column commands

Each phrase row has three effect columns: a command and a hex value. The info line at the bottom of the screen explains the one under the cursor.

CSLMIDI CC glide: the CCA–CCD commands on the same row move to their value over XY ticks instead of jumping (00: across the step), from the value sent before
DIRplay direction for this track from the next row on: 00 forward, 01 backwards, 02 ping-pong, 03 a random row each step (a phrase still lasts as many steps as it has rows)
BYP…chains module X (the number on its BYP button; 0 = all) in (Y 0), bypassed (Y 1), or the other way from the patch for Y rows then back
FXOeffect slot X (0 = all) off (XY with Y 0), on (Y 1), or on for Y rows then back
FXSpick what FXV moves on this track: slot X (1–8), its parameter Y (1–F, in the FX screen's order)
FXVset that parameter, 00 its lowest – FF its highest (the slot's own value comes back when the song stops)
SCAthis track's scale from here on: X the root (0 = C … B), Y the scale (0 off, 1 major, 2 minor, 3 harmonic minor…); KEY FOLLOW instruments
SCGevery track's scale from here on, as SCA
CUTlow-pass the pad from here on, 00 dark – FF off
FDIfade the note in over XX ticks
TRMtremolo on the note: X cycles a beat, Y depth
APNauto-pan the note: X cycles a beat, Y width
TVLthis track's level from here on, 00 silent – FF the mixer's (back at stop)
TPNthis track's pan from here on, 80 centre (back at stop)
STPstop every note: 00 this track, 01 every track
LPBlines per beat for every track from here on (00 the phrases' own)
PDLthe whole song waits XX rows
ONEone note of the row's chord, at random
MPBMIDI pitch bend, 80 centre
MATMIDI channel pressure
RESresonance for CUT
DECshorten the pad from here on, 00 a click – FF its own length
FLXFlex pattern: 00 off, 01–10
GATStep gate pattern: 00 custom, 01–0F
RTGretrigger every X (1 = 1/4 … 5 = 1/64, 6–8 triplets) for Y rows; 00 stops
ARParpeggio: the note, +X, +Y semitones
ARCarpeggio pattern (X) and speed in ticks (Y)
CHAchance the note plays
PRBchance the command to its left happens (as RND changes it; with none, the note's chance)
MUTplay variation XX of the pad's sound (INST › RANGE: how far); RND or RNL after it for a new one each time
GENplay a fresh sound XX of the instrument's GEN TYPE (INST › GEN TYPE, FAMILY, RANGE)
DELdelay the note by XX ticks
GRVgroove for this track: X ticks even, Y odd
GGRgroove for every track
HOPend the phrase; the next starts at row Y
INSplay with instrument XX
KILstop the note after XX ticks
OFFfade the note out after XX ticks
NTHplay on pass Y of every X
RETretrigger every Y ticks, X fades
REPrepeat the last command, adding XX
RNDrandomise the command to the left
RNLRND as a random walk
PSLslide from the last pitch
PBNbend the pitch across the step
PVBvibrato: X speed, Y depth
SEDseed the random numbers
TPOtempo in BPM
TICticks a step from here on (00: the project’s)
TSPtranspose the track from here on
VOLvolume
PITpitch in semitones (signed)
FINfine tune in cents
PLY00 forwards, 01 reversed
STAstart point into the sound
PANpan, 80 is centre
WOBbass wobble rate from here on: 01 4 bars, 02 2 bars, 03 1 bar, 04 1/2, 05 1/2T, 06 1/4, 07 1/4T, 08 1/8D, 09 1/8, 0A 1/8T, 0B 1/16, 0C 1/16T, 0D 1/32; 00 the voice’s own
CCA–CCDMIDI CC: 00–7F to the instrument’s CC slot A–D (the CC numbers are on INST)
PGMMIDI program change 00–7F, just before the row’s note

MIDI instruments (INST › OUTPUT MIDI or PAD+MIDI) send to their PORT A–D: ⚙ Settings → MIDI (on a computer, Audio & MIDI ▾ in the top bar) says which cable each letter is on this device, so a song plays the same on the phone and the computer. CCA–CCD and PGM work on rows without a note too (on the track’s last instrument), and RND, RNL and REP change them like any command. PSL, PBN, PVB, PIT/FIN on a held note and fractions of a semitone are sent as pitch bend: set INST › BEND RANGE to the range your gear bends. ARP plays its steps as notes, then the note itself again (unless the next row retunes it or plays another note).

LFO → CC: INST › LFO CC (set a CC number) runs an LFO on that CC while the song plays: SHAPE, RATE in time with the song (T triplet, D dotted), DEPTH (127 is the whole range), CENTRE, and RESTART (FREE from PLAY, NOTE at each of the instrument’s notes). Song position: with clock out on, playing the song from a row partway into a block sends Song Position Pointer and Continue, so the gear starts at the same place; with clock in on, the other device’s Continue after a Song Position Pointer plays the song from there.

Playing and recording from a MIDI keyboard: ⚙ Settings → MIDI → Keys play: in the tracker the keyboard plays the instrument you're on (the INST screen's, or the cursor row's in a phrase) and holds it while the key is down; a MIDI instrument plays its gear, with bend, aftertouch, sustain and every unlearned knob passed through. Notes in picks the input and channel, Clock from the input Clock in follows, and each port has its own delay. REC on the top strip (F9): stopped, a note or chord goes in at the cursor and the cursor moves on when you let go; playing, notes land on the step they were played on in the track under the cursor, with velocity and OFFs (a take is one undo step). CLICK is the metronome; Settings → Record & play has its level, the count-in, REC TIMING (STEP, or TICKS: the step plus a DEL) and LIVE TRANSPOSE (a key transposes the KEY FOLLOW instruments as the song plays).

More for sequencing: on a poly track each note column is its own MIDI voice. INST › NOTE LEN ends a MIDI instrument's notes after some ticks; ECHO repeats them on the gear (time, fade, pitch per repeat); KEY FOLLOW instruments follow the song's SCALE (Project → Song) and live transpose; HUMAN TIME and HUMAN VEL vary each note. CSL makes a row's CC commands glide; DIR plays a track backwards, ping-pong or at random. Edit ▾ → Euclidean fill… spreads hits evenly over steps. File ▾ → Export MIDI file writes the song as a .mid (drum pads on channel 10) and Import MIDI file… brings one in as phrases. There are 64 instruments (00–3F).

The master column (MST)

On the Song screen, the amber MST column after the poly tracks plays phrases whose commands drive the master bus: VOL sets the master level from that row on, and FXO, FLX, GAT and RTG work on the master's effects (Mixer → master → FX). Master phrases are their own kind: just the three command columns (no notes, volume or instrument), and the command list offers only what works on the master: VOL, FXO, FXS, FXV, FLX, GAT, RTG, then TPO, TIC, LPB, PDL, GGR, SCG, HOP, DEL, STP, CHA, PRB, NTH, REP, RND, RNL and SED. Beside the grid on a big screen, the master's effect chain shows instead of the piano. It plays alongside the tracks, block by block, and is not shown in Arrange. Stopping puts the master level and every switched effect back as set.

Momentary effects: put an effect in a slot and leave it off, then FXO 21 switches slot 2 on, FXO 20 off again, or FXO 24 turns it on for four rows. It works on any track (that track's slots) and in the MST column (the master's). Switching fades over 5 ms; Flex keeps listening while it is off, so it always has the last bar ready.

…chains modules: every effect module in a …chains patch has a BYP button on its title bar with a number: it bypasses the module (its dry sound passes). From a phrase, BYP 31 bypasses module 3 on that track's chain, BYP 30 puts it back, and BYP 34 switches it the other way from the patch for four rows, so a trance gate left bypassed plays for four rows. BYP 0Y does every numbered module. Stopping the song puts them back as the patch has them.

Presets and sidechains in …chains: effects and sound sources have a Preset row: factory presets, Default, and your own (Save as a preset keeps them on this device, for every patch). Every sidechain user has a Source: Self, Send 1–8 (what a Sidechain Out in any chain sends) or one track's own sound, before its effects and fader, so a muted ghost kick still drives it. That goes for Sidechain In (its meter shows what it hears before you patch it), Sidechain Comp, the compressors, the noise gate and the envelope filter, in …chains and as track or master effects. The Mixer's SC row lights when a track is a source for something. The light beside a module's SC input flashes with the sidechain it hears.

Flex, Step gate and Retrigger

Flex re-sequences the last bar in time with the song: repeats, fills, a stutter build, half speed, tape stop, reversed beats, a backspin, scratching, gates, shuffles, a beat juggle, octave-up and random slices (16 patterns; FLX picks one from a row). Step gate is a 16-step gate in time with the song: 15 patterns, or CUSTOM from two hex bytes (STEPS 1-8 and 9-16, a 1 bit is an open step); GAT picks. Retrigger catches a slice when it starts and repeats it, each repeat quieter (DECAY) or pitched (PITCH): RTG 32 repeats 1/16 slices for two rows, or set MODE to ALWAYS and switch it with FXO. All three follow the song's tempo and bar (they pass the sound through when the song is stopped). Each command needs its effect in one of the track's (or the master's) slots: type FLX, GAT or RTG where it's missing and it is added to the first free slot.

Track effects

Each track and the master have 8 effect slots (FX screen, or the Mixer’s FX row): 72 effects on a track and 81 on a bus or the master (with the nine …pump ones; …pump EQ goes on any track), in groups: dynamics and EQ (compressors, Bus and Glue Comp, limiter, noise gate, transient shaper, multiband, air), filters (filter, ladder, low and high cut, auto-wah, vowel, envelope filter), drive and lo-fi (saturation, drive, overdrive, tube, tape, wavefolder, bitcrush, lo-fi, degrade, vinyl, dub tape, cab), modulation (chorus, ensemble, dimension, flanger, phaser, tremolo, auto-pan, rotary, ring mod, cross-mod, frequency shifter), delays (simple, tape, BBD, pitch, granular, reverse echo), reverbs (room, plate, spring, space, Galactic, pitch reverb, convolution), pitch and voice (pitch shifter, harmonizer, pitch correct), resonators (resonator, comb, Rings), spectral and granular (Clouds, Beads, spectral, extreme stretch), rhythmic (Flex, Step gate, Retrigger, trance gate, pump, Beat grains, Beat scramble, Glitch sequencer) and utility (stereo width, utility). The pad's Add effect menu has 65 of them. On the Mixer’s FX row, OPTION (Alt in KEYS mode) + ▲▶ turns a track's effects on in order, up to eight, and OPTION + ▼◀ turns the last one off without losing its settings — turn the count back up and it returns; with none on, slots fill from 1. EDIT on the row opens the FX screen. Renders include them; stems skip the master effects and limiter. For drums and IDM: Beat grains (a rhythmic grain cloud in time with the song, after Output Portal: rate, density, size, position, spray, pitch and random pitch, reverse, shape, stereo, freeze), Beat scramble (re-orders the last bar's slices, some reversed; keep the beats, new every bar or looped) and Glitch sequencer (each step may stutter, reverse, jump an octave, tape-stop, crush or drop out). Under a slot's controls, › PRESET lists INIT, factory presets (over 230 across the effects) and the song's own, and › SAVE AS PRESET… keeps the slot's settings for that effect. › EQ WINDOW (at the bottom of the FX screen, on any track) opens the track's …pump EQ in its own window, adding one to a free slot if needed; …pump EQ works on every track, the other …pump effects on buses and the master.

The FX screen keeps the slot list and the open slot's controls apart: ▲▼ move within one of the two, and ◀▶ (or a sideways swipe) open the slot under the cursor and go back to the list — so scrolling never changes the effect you are editing. A filled slot shows ›, and the open one shows ▪.

…chains (the modular effects screen) is live: adding or removing a module, moving a cable, or turning a slider is heard at once — no need to restart playback. Its Resample module records what passes through it into a pad, starting on the next bar, and slices it so you can chop it like a breakbeat.

Synth page

Z–/ · Q–PPlay the selected pad chromatically; C-4 is its own pitch. On a synth slot (9–16) notes hold while the keys are down, so you can play chords
− =Octave down / up
Shift 1–8 or ◀ ▶Pick a pad (◀▶ go through all 16 slots; on a computer, where they are a list down the left, ▲▼ do too)
Shift SpacePlay the pad as it is (Space plays or stops the song, as everywhere)
Alt 1–7Jump into a tracker screen
Alt 8 · 9 · 0 · `…waves · …chains · the synth · back to the last view (these and Alt+1–7 work from …waves and …chains too)

Presets: the list beside the pad name loads a whole sound. It starts with one group per drum type (Kicks, Snares, Claps & snaps, Rims & sticks, Closed hats, Open hats, Cymbals, Toms, Hand drums, Shakers & tambourines, Cowbells, blocks & metal), gathering every drum the app has from its own designs, the drum engines and the classic and acoustic kits; then IDM and glitch hits, basses, pads, chords, keys, leads and each engine's sounds. The search box finds any of them by name. ＋ Save this as a preset… keeps the pad in this song's own list, at the top; it travels in the project file. The Layer presets list in the layer card swaps just the selected layer (a snare's noise, a clicky pitch sweep…) and keeps it at the right pitch on any pad. File ▾ → Export song presets… / Import presets… moves them between songs and devices; Save kit / Load kit moves all 16 pads at once. Drum kits… (File ▾, or ⚙ Settings → Kit) puts a CR-78-, 808-, 606-, 909-, 707-, 727- or 505-style kit, or a clean acoustic kit (Funk, Studio, Jazz), on pads 1–8 and keeps the synth slots; every sound of each kit is also in the Presets list, filed under its type (808 Kick under Kicks). Funk breaks… (File ▾) loads one of twelve original breaks, with swing, ghost notes and a laid-back snare, as a new song with its acoustic kit, or adds its four bars to this song. Breaks to chop (File ▾) has the fourteen breaks of …pump BREAK, rendered by its own kit with room and tape, as a one-bar loop in a slot, cut into 16 slices (C-4 plays slice 1) and synced to the tempo, ready to re-sequence. Acid line… (Edit ▾ or right-click on a phrase) writes a random bass line into the phrase the way …pump ACID does — scale, root, density, accents, slides and octave jumps; Roll (R) again or Mutate (M) a few steps, and light only the lanes you want changed — for an Acid pad (accents are volume FF, slides PSL).

Voice pitch, filter & amp (in the card under the pad name) shape the whole voice at once, across every layer: a pitch envelope, a low-pass filter with its own envelope, and an amp envelope. Each envelope has an Amount slider setting how far it is applied. The layer card's Filter and Amp sections still shape only the selected layer.

Mod matrix (Voice card): 3 LFOs (rate, shape, depth), 3 envelopes (A/D/S/R) and a 32-step sequencer, each routed to one destination — pitch, level, low-pass cutoff or high-pass cutoff — with a signed amount, applied across all of the voice's layers. Every amount starts at zero. Turn it up and sweep a filter, wobble the pitch, or shape the level. Mod envelopes has a Reset to defaults button that puts the pitch, amp and the three mod envelopes back to their factory values.

Voice play: Glide slides the pitch from the last note; Mono + Legato retunes the sounding note instead of retriggering. Tuning (song) is a cents offset per pitch class (Equal, Just, Pythagorean and Meantone presets or your own), applied to live playing and the tracker. The Wavetable oscillator (Position/Formant) and its Bend/Unison/Spread/Sub/Noise sit in the layer card when that type is picked.

Engine (synth slots): Layers is the layer synth above; Bass swaps in the bass engine and Voice a singing voice that sings typed lyrics, and Blip (on any pad) a minimal electronic drum (see Bass, Voice and Blip engine on the Start tab). Acid is a mono bass-line synth (saw or square into a squelchy ladder filter): a note with a volume of C0 or more is accented, and PSL slides. Machine is a mono synth with seven machines (Dual VCO, Chip, FM+, Swarm, Ensemble, Noise, Additive), each with its own A, B and C, then high- and low-pass filters, an amp envelope and an LFO. Both play live in the tracker. Tone drum is a modelled drum (a tone with a pitch bend or an inharmonic spectrum, filtered noise with a sweep, a click, distortion), and Modal a struck, plucked, bowed or blown object (bar, marimba, vibes, glock, bell, gong, membrane, glass, string, tube, wood, plate). Piano is a modelled struck string (hammer hardness, strike point, two or three detuned strings, string stiffness, soundboard, dampers and a sustain pedal); Tine EP a suitcase-style electric piano (tine and tone bar, a growling pickup you set with Bark, the hammer's bell, tremolo); Organ a tonewheel organ with nine drawbars, percussion, key click, a rotary speaker and Pluck, which with the House organ (M1 style) preset gives the classic 90s house organ. SoundFont plays any .sf2 / .sf3 file you load, or General MIDI (FluidR3 Mono, MIT, downloaded once, 24 MB): pick the preset from the list (bank 128 is the drum kits); the tracker plays it key by key from the font (C-4 is middle C, C-2 the GM kick), with the font's own envelopes, filters and loops. Swarm is a cloud of up to 48 detuned oscillators, each drifting on its own (Cohesion makes them drift together), with Scatter onto octaves, fifths or chords, Bloom (voices fade in one by one), Shimmer, a morphing wave, a resonant filter with its own envelope and an ADSR; it holds for as long as the tracker note. Drift is a two-line analog pad synth laid out like the big 1970s CS-series polysynths (two oscillator lines per voice, a high-pass and a low-pass with their own envelope, up to four drifting unison voices) followed by a tape stage — Wow and Flutter on the pitch, chorus, saturation, Age (worn top and bottom, the odd dropout) and hiss — for warm, wobbly, faded pads; its presets are in the pad Presets list under Drift (tape pads). …pump (group in the engine list) has the pump plugins' instruments with their own sound and presets: Mono (three oscillators, four filters), Poly (two oscillators, poly-mod, unison, chorus) and Coil (tuned springs kicked by the note). Each renders a note like the other engines (Hit is how hard it is played), and each has a live twin that plays the plugin in the tracker note by note, with the VOL column as velocity, slides and bends as pitch bend, and glide (Coil live also sets how many Voices ring at once, 1–16). A twin shares its values with the rendered engine; if the device can't keep up, the live ones fall back to their renders and say so (Settings → Audio → …pump live). On a poly track (9–16) a Voice pad sings chords: notes that start together sing the same syllable in harmony. In ⚙ Settings: Audio (output, level, latency and Reset audio engine, which clears a stuck note or effect), Project (song, input, Render & export — WAVs for Koala and SunVox — and Mastering), Screen (the tracker's screen and arrange settings, and the Skin), then Kit, MIDI connects a controller (notes not mapped to a pad play the selected synth slot, held until note-off) and App.

Files and rendering

File ▾ holds Save, Save As and Open, plus Render song (a stereo WAV, through the mastering chain when it is on) and Render stems (a zip with the mix and one WAV per track, without mastering), plus New song, Load demo song, kit save and load, and sharing. In desktop Chrome and Edge, Save writes straight back to the file you opened or last saved; other browsers download a copy, and Save As asks for a name first. The song also saves itself in the browser as you work.

More detail in the README on GitHub.
